data.narrative:
Atlas Motion, a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by former Shield AI and Mach Industries executives (Mochen, Baron, Dela Rosa), has raised $11.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparables universe of nine private robotics firms and one public peer (277810.KQ), though narrow peer matching proved limited for multi-method triangulation.

Stage-progression analysis, the primary applicable method, uses the $11.5M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage progression, yielding $29M. A formal peer-median approach was inapplicable due to insufficient narrow comparables—while the robotics sector contains ten same-sector peers, none met the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier clustering needed for robust median derivation. Relying on all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the specialized nature of frontier-tech robotics.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $24M (low) to $33M (high), centered on $29M. This range reflects typical seed-to-series-A step-up dynamics but carries material uncertainty given the single-method foundation. Key variables include revenue traction and technical validation milestones not captured in this dataset, management team credibility from prior exits, and the trajectory of comparables like Walden Robotics and Divergent. Additional data on Atlas Motion's runway, customer commitments, or technology differentiation would materially refine this estimate.
